sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: n = 400, sample proportion 55%. Margin and interval?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 14 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 1.4% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 1.4% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 54 and standard deviation 6. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 42 and 66?
A researcher runs an observational study of volunteers who chose their own group. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 55%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 2 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 67 and standard deviation 20. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 27 and 107?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
